Each answer lands as a step card — title, caption, visual — plus what morphs from one step into the next.
Same shapes, new beats. Every answer extends the story without redrawing it.
Spell out every step, or sketch a few and see how it looks. You hold the gate.
Your steps are wired into one evolving scene, drawn with a shared scene kit — ready-made boxes, arrows, and motion that make entities morph.
Before saying done, it builds and renders every step — and fixes what breaks.
Point at a step and ask. The skill edits the scene in place — nothing is redrawn from scratch.
This presentation was built exactly this way. Thanks for watching.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its step table to the shared Presentation API. The shared Stage renders each step’s Scene, and the demo’s ReferenceScene builds its diagram with scene-kit nodes and Presence.

demo-integration.rationale: The nine entries generated from the content table all use ReferenceScene and the same groupKey. Stage keys the host by that groupKey, preserving its mount across these steps. Separately, presentation-owned ENTITY values and cardId supply stable node IDs; the node primitives pass those IDs to Motion as layoutId.

evidence: Its readiness loop accepts a successful fetch from port 4173 without checking the spawned child's exit or its own ready output. The root verifier has child checks, but the delivered bootstrap ver…

evidence: The failure test injects a render exception and asserts only nonzero status and 'step 1'; it does not inject a console error or assert that the browser error propagates.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier fails when navigation does not reach the next step, and a focused test asserts the failing step number.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project provides a separate inspect command that starts a local preview and writes per-step screenshots.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper loops through reported steps, but the executable test does not prove that every produced screenshot comes from the intended preview.
evidence: The screenshot test uses page.setContent and manually changes data-step-index; it never invokes the preview-backed inspect command against a produced presentation.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture waits a fixed number of milliseconds without observing animation completion or sharing a transition contract with runtime motion.
evidence: captureSettledStep calls waitForTimeout(settleMs) before screenshot; the integration test only waits longer than its fixture's timer.

verification-tooling.rationale: The focused test covers flat sibling text collisions, but the detector does not inspect representative nested text and chrome or preserve collisions involving an unrelated element beside an allowed overlap.
evidence: The detector filters to leaf elements and suppresses a collision whenever either element has a data-allow-overlap ancestor; the test contains no marked-versus-unrelated collision.

verification-tooling.rationale: The overlap exemption is too broad: marking one element suppresses collisions with unrelated elements outside the marked region.
evidence: The collision condition requires neither element to have a data-allow-overlap ancestor. The test verifies suppression within one marked group and detection of a separate unmarked pair, but not preser…

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares rendered active and inactive control styles, and a browser fixture verifies the warning when they match.
evidence: inspectStep compares computed color, background, border, opacity, and weight; the integration test creates matching active and inactive progress buttons and asserts the active-state warning.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper warns for absent, undersized, or browser-default attribution, and a browser fixture verifies the warning for a default-styled link.
evidence: inspectStep checks attribution presence, computed font size, and default blue underlined styling; the test supplies an unstyled attribution anchor and asserts the warning text.
